content: 1. Clarithromycin increases the plasma concentration and pharmacological effects of indinavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction necessitates avoiding the combination or using an alternative drug. 2. Indinavir increases the levels and effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Indinavir elevates colchicine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing guidelines. Colchicine is a substrate of both P-gp and CYP3A4, and its use with strong inhibitors of both pathways is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 4. Indinavir increases copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 5. Indinavir increases dabrafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Indinavir increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Indinavir increases darifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Dexlansoprazole reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both drugs. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 9. Indinavir increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Indinavir increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Dronedarone also increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 11. Efavirenz reduces indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Indinavir increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Indinavir increases elbasvir/grazoprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Eliglustat increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of the P-gp substrate. 15. Indinavir and elivaldogene autotemcel may mutually reduce each other's effects. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 16. Indinavir increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 17. Indinavir increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Indinavir increases encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 19. Indinavir increases entrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, resume the prior entrectinib dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 20. Indinavir increases enzalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while enzalutamide reduces indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Indinavir increases erdafitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 22. Indinavir increases ergoloid mesylates levels by inhibiting metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Indinavir increases ergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Erythromycin base increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases erythromycin base levels by the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases erythromycin stearate levels by the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Esomeprazole reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both drugs. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Indinavir and ethinyl estradiol may interact, leading to significant changes in estrogen plasma levels. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method. 30. Etravirine reduces indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination unless indinavir is boosted with low-dose ritonavir. 31. Indinavir increases everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Famotidine reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both drugs. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Indinavir increases fedratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 34. Indinavir increases felbamate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Indinavir increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 36. Indinavir reduces fexinidazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while fexinidazole increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 37. Indinavir increases fluticasone intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, such as Cushing syndrome. 38. Indinavir increases gilteritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects and adjust the dosage as needed. 39. Indinavir increases glasdegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 40. Indinavir increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Indinavir increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 42. Ibuprofen/famotidine reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both drugs. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Indinavir increases idelalisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministered, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed. 44. Indinavir increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and reducing metabolism via UGT1A1 inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 45. Indinavir increases irinotecan liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and reducing metabolism via UGT1A1 inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 46. Indinavir increases ivosidenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg/day. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg/day. 47. Lansoprazole reduces indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both drugs. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 48. Indinavir increases larotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%.
